title: macOS: Implement additional accessibility methods
body: Fixes #9932; also see https://github.com/ghostty-org/ghostty/discussions/9930. **Submitting this as a draft PR to get feedback on the areas listed below. Please let me know whether this is going in the right direction.** - The code was largely written by Claude Code, with guidance from me. I have read through the implementation and reviewed it; overall, the code looks reasonable to me. (I have of course also checked that it actually works; see below.) I have also improved the factoring and removed some unnecessary duplication etc., especially on the Swift side. - I have read the contribution guidelines and AI policy, but it still leaves room for interpretation (e.g. with regards to how many comments are "too much" etc., see below); happy to make adjustments to bring this further in line with your expectations. Again, this is just a rough first draft. - I have intentionally left in most comments (and asked Claude to focus on the _motivation_ of the code); happy to clean them up further if you find them too verbose. - Caveat: I have hardly any experience with Zig, so I may have missed something in that implementation. In particular, my knowledge of PinMap is limited, so please feel free to provide some guidance there (see below). - Speaking of PinMap, I am unsure how inefficient the current implementation is in practice. But even if it is somewhat inefficient, it could serve as a starting point for a more efficient implementation as needed in practice. - To my understanding, we could also replace `cachedScreenContents` and `cachedVisibleContents` with accesses into the `cachedScreenTextInfo`; I also don't think they are accessed much more frequently than the `cachedScreenTextInfo`, so any possible performance overhead of `cachedScreenTextInfo` would probably be tolerable. Happy to make these changes, let me know. - Speaking of `cachedVisibleContents`, I am unsure why reading the visible text with `ghostty_surface_read_text` would be less expensive (potentially by not requiring a PinMap, but how?) than getting byte offsets into the entire text using a PinMap. - As an alternative, maybe we could include a pointer to a PinMap itself in the `cachedScreenTextInfo` struct and cache that, to minimize the frequency of recreating PinMaps for Accessibility methods? That could be worthwhile to also optimize the other AX methods (e.g. for getting the rectangles of certain characters etc.). We would probably need to manage the PinMap's lifetime in Swift, but I guess that's doable. - @mitchellh your feedback on how we should best architect this aspect, both from a caching and a Swift/Zig interop perspective, would be greatly appreciated. - Tests are only on the Zig layer right now; having good tests on the Swift layer might be a bit more difficult because we'd need to test them in the UI harness (haven't looked too much into that yet). - Not _all_ Accessibility methods have been implemented yet, but hopefully a subset that already provides value; most others (e.g. selected text range, notifications for that) would add slightly less value and I already feel like this PR is getting large enough. - As Accessibility implementations also very much depend on how AX clients actually interact with this API (and what they expect from it), it would be useful to get feedback from actual users of AX clients. /cc @grishy @burakssen - For reference, I did use my own app [Cotypist](https://cotypist.app) (which also uses AX extensively) to see whether the implementation is sufficient for it. Will attach a screenshot of the result shortly; overall, it looks decent, but there's room for improvement. But I felt it was good to first get some feedback on the current state. - Screenshot: Completions are shown in roughly the right location: - `macos/tools/check-accessibility/` tool: Pure AI slop, but very useful for debugging/verifying the implementation; happy to remove it from the PR before leaving draft status; let me know. --- _AI slop (but guided by me in an attempt to make it actually useful) follows_ # PR: Implement rich macOS accessibility for terminal surfaces ## Overview Adds comprehensive macOS Accessibility support so VoiceOver and other assistive technologies can read terminal content, navigate by line, locate characters spatially, and stay in sync as new output arrives. The implementation spans the full stack: Zig core terminal logic, the C API bridge, and the Swift/AppKit accessibility overrides. All positional data flows as **UTF-8 byte offsets** from the Zig core. The Swift layer converts to/from **UTF-16 code units** (NSRange semantics) at the boundary, since every macOS Accessibility API speaks NSRange. ## Accessibility functions | Override | Purpose | How it works | |---|---|---| | `accessibilityValue` | Full terminal text (scrollback + active) | Reads from `ScreenTextInfo` cache, which calls `ghostty_surface_ax_text` to get text + viewport byte range via the Zig pin map | | `accessibilityNumberOfCharacters` | Total character count | `NSString.length` (UTF-16 code units) on the cached text | | `accessibilityVisibleCharacterRange` | Viewport range within the full text | Zig core walks its pin map to find viewport start/end byte offsets; Swift converts to an NSRange via `String.Index` | | `accessibilityLine(for:)` | Line number for a UTF-16 character index | Converts the UTF-16 index to a `String.Index`, slices, counts newlines | | `accessibilityRange(forLine:)` | Character range for a line number | Walks UTF-16 code units via `NSString.character(at:)` counting `\n` boundaries | | `accessibilityInsertionPointLineNumber` | Cursor's line number | Gets cursor byte offset from Zig (`ax_cursor_offset`), counts `0x0A` bytes directly in UTF-8 — safe because no multi-byte sequence contains `0x0A` | | `accessibilityFrame(for:)` | Screen-coordinate bounds of a character range (AXBoundsForRange) | Converts NSRange → UTF-8 byte offset, asks Zig for cell bounds, flips Y from top-left to AppKit bottom-left, converts view → screen coords. Same-line ranges get a tight rect; multi-line ranges use full view width (matching NSTextView/Terminal.app behavior) | | `accessibilityRange(for:)` | Character at a screen point (AXRangeForPosition) | Converts screen → window → view → flipped-Y coordinates, asks Zig for the byte offset at that grid position, converts back to a 1-character NSRange | | `accessibilityContentDidChange` | Notifies VoiceOver of new output | Invalidates the text cache and posts `NSAccessibility.valueChanged`. Triggered by a push-based `content_changed` action from the renderer — no polling | ## Changes by layer ### Zig core — `src/terminal/Screen.zig` New `AccessibilityText` and `AccessibilityCell` types, plus four functions: - **`accessibilityText`** — Builds a full-screen selection, generates text with a `PinMap`, then scans the map to find the viewport's start/end byte offsets using a node-to-row-offset hash map. - **`accessibilityGridForOffset`** — Resolves a byte offset to a viewport-relative `(col, row)` cell via the pin map. Returns `null` for offsets in scrollback above the viewport. - **`accessibilityOffsetForGrid`** — Inverse: resolves viewport `(col, row)` to a byte offset. Falls back to row-start if the exact column has no content (e.g. cursor past end of line). - **`accessibilityCursorOffset`** — Convenience wrapper that calls `accessibilityOffsetForGrid` with the current cursor coordinates. Includes 17 unit tests covering scrollback, wide characters, soft wraps, empty screens, round-trips, and edge cases. ### Surface — `src/Surface.zig` Thin wrappers that lock the renderer mutex and delegate to `Screen`. `boundsForOffset` also handles content-scale conversion (pixels ↔ points) and wide-character cell widths. ### C API — `include/ghostty.h`, `src/apprt/embedded.zig` Five new exports: - `ghostty_surface_ax_text` / `_ax_text_free` — text + viewport byte range - `ghostty_surface_ax_bounds` — byte offset → view-local cell rect - `ghostty_surface_ax_offset` — view-local point → byte offset - `ghostty_surface_ax_cursor_offset` — cursor byte offset New `ghostty_ax_text_s` and `ghostty_ax_bounds_s` structs. All offsets are UTF-8 bytes; the docstrings note that platform layers using NSRange must convert. ### Action / Message — `src/apprt/action.zig`, `src/apprt/surface.zig` New `content_changed` action and surface message, replacing the previous polling approach. ### Renderer — `src/renderer/generic.zig` When the terminal's dirty flag is set, pushes a `content_changed` message through the surface mailbox (instant/non-blocking, like the scrollbar notification). ### Swift / macOS — `SurfaceView_AppKit.swift`, `Ghostty.App.swift` - New `ScreenTextInfo` struct with `viewportRange` (NSRange), `utf16Length`, `utf8Offset(of:)`, and `characterIndex(forUTF8Offset:)` helpers. - Separate `cachedScreenTextInfo` cache (500ms TTL) — kept distinct from `cachedScreenContents` because the pin-map-based text generation is more expensive and only needed by accessibility callers. - `CachedValue` gains an `invalidate()` method for push-based cache busting. - `Ghostty.App` dispatches the `content_changed` action to `surfaceView.accessibilityContentDidChange()`. ### Test tool — `macos/tools/check-accessibility/` Standalone Swift Package Manager CLI that queries a running Ghostty instance via the macOS AX API. Dumps all text-area attributes and parameterized attributes (bounds, ranges, line navigation), runs automated consistency checks, and supports `--listen` mode for monitoring `valueChanged`/`selectedTextChanged` notifications in real time.
